# PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION

## This Practice Direction supplements Section IV of CPR Part 6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > This Practice Direction supplements Section IV of CPR Part 6] Contents of this Practice Direction

## Scope of this Practice Direction

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Scope of this Practice Direction] 1.1 This Practice Direction supplements Section IV (service of the claim form and other documents out of the jurisdiction) of Part 6. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Scope of this Practice Direction] (Practice Direction 6A contains relevant provisions supplementing rule 6.40 in relation to the method of service on a party in Scotland or Northern Ireland.)

## Service out of the jurisdiction where permission of the court is not required

## 2.1 Where rule 6.34 applies, the claimant must file practice form N510 when filing the claim form. ## Service out of the jurisdiction where permission is required

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service out of the jurisdiction where permission is required] 3.1 The claimant may serve a claim form out of the jurisdiction with the permission of the court under rule 6.36 where –

## General Grounds

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (1) A claim is made for a remedy against a person domiciled within the jurisdiction within the meaning of sections 41 and 42 of the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (1A) A claim is made against a person in respect of a dispute arising out of the operations of a branch, agency or other establishment of that person within the jurisdiction, but only if proceedings cannot be served on the branch, agency or establishment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (2) A claim is made for an injunction(GL) ordering the defendant to do or refrain from doing an act within the jurisdiction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (3) A claim is made against a person (‘the defendant’) on whom the claim form has been or will be served (otherwise than in reliance on this paragraph) and –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (a) there is between the claimant and the defendant a real issue which it is reasonable for the court to try; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (b) the claimant wishes to serve the claim form on another person who is a necessary or proper party to that claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (4) A claim is an additional claim under Part 20 and the person to be served is a necessary or proper party to the claim or additional claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (4A) A claim is made against the defendant which—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (a) was served  on the defendant within the jurisdiction without the need for the defendant’s agreement to accept such service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (b) falls within CPR rule 6.33; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > General Grounds] (c) falls within one or more of paragraphs (1A), (2), (6) to (16A) or (19) to (23),and a further claim is made against the same defendant which arises out of the same or closely connected facts. ## Claims for interim remedies

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for interim remedies] (5) A claim is made for an interim remedy under section 25(1) of the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982. ## Claims in relation to contracts

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (6) A claim is made in respect of a contract where the contract –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (a) was (i) made within the jurisdiction or (ii) concluded by the acceptance of an offer, which offer was received within the jurisdiction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (b) was made by or through an agent trading or residing within the jurisdiction or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (c) is governed by the law of England and Wales. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (7) A claim is made in respect of a breach of contract committed, or likely to be committed within the jurisdiction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (8) A claim is made for a declaration that no contract exists where, if the contract was found to exist, it would comply with the conditions set out in paragraph (6). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (8A)A claim for unlawfully causing or assisting in:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (a) a breach of a contract where the contract falls within one of paragraphs (6)(a) to (6)(c) above or within Rule 6.33(2B); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in relation to contracts] (b) a breach of contract falling within paragraph (7) above. ## Claims in tort

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in tort] (9) A claim is made in tort where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in tort] (a) damage was sustained, or will be sustained, within the jurisdiction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in tort] (b) damage which has been or will be sustained results from an act committed, or likely to be committed, within the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims in tort] (c) the claim is governed by the law of England and Wales. ## Enforcement

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Enforcement] (10) A claim is made to enforce any judgment or arbitral award. ## Claims about property within the jurisdiction

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about property within the jurisdiction] (11) The subject matter of the claim relates wholly or principally to property within the jurisdiction, provided that nothing under this paragraph shall render justiciable the title to or the right to possession of immovable property outside England and Wales. ## Claims about trusts etc. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (12) A claim is made in respect of a trust which is created by the operation of a statute, or by a written instrument, or created orally and evidenced in writing, and which is governed by the law of England and Wales. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (12A) A claim is made in respect of a trust which is created by the operation of a statute, or by a written instrument, or created orally and evidenced in writing, and which provides that jurisdiction in respect of such a claim shall be conferred upon the courts of England and Wales. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (12B)A claim is made in respect of a trust which is created by the operation of a statute, or by a written instrument, or created orally and evidenced in writing, and which expressly or impliedly designates England and Wales as the principal place of administration. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (12C)  A claim is made in respect of a trust created in the jurisdiction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (12D)  A claim is made for a declaration that no trust has arisen where, if the trust was found to have arisen, it would comply with one of the conditions set out in paragraph (12), (12A), (12B) or (12C). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (12E)A claim is made for a breach of trust where the breach is committed or likely to be within the jurisdiction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (13) A claim is made for any remedy which might be obtained in proceedings for the administration of the estate of a person who died domiciled within the jurisdiction or whose estate includes assets within the jurisdiction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (14) A probate claim or a claim for the rectification of a will. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (15) A claim is made against the defendant as constructive trustee, or as trustee of a resulting trust, where the claim—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (a)  arises out of acts committed or events occurring within the jurisdiction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (b) relates to assets within the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (c) is governed by the law of England and Wales. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (15A)A claim for unlawfully causing or assisting in—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (a) a breach of a trust where the trust falls within one of paragraphs (12) to (12C) above;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (b) a breach of trust falling within paragraph (12E) above; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (c) a breach of a constructive or resulting trust where the trustee’s liability would fall within paragraph (15) above. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (15B)A claim is made for breach of fiduciary duty, where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (a)the breach is committed, or likely to be committed, within the jurisdiction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (b)  the fiduciary duty arose in the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (c)  the fiduciary duty is governed by the law of England and Wales. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (15C)A claim for unlawfully causing or assisting in—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (a) a breach of fiduciary duty where the fiduciary duty falls within one of paragraph (15B)(b) or (c) above;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (b) a breach of fiduciary duty falling within paragraph (15A)(a) above. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (15D)  A claim is made for a declaration that no fiduciary duty has arisen where, if the fiduciary duty was found to have arisen, it would comply with  one of the conditions set out in paragraph (15B)(b) or (c). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (16) A claim is made for restitution where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (a) the defendant’s alleged liability arises out of acts committed within the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (b) the enrichment is obtained within the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims about trusts etc.] (c) the claim is governed by the law of England and Wales. ## Declarations of non-liability

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Declarations of non-liability] (16A) A claim is made for a declaration that the claimant is not liable where, if a claim were brought against the  claimant seeking to establish that liability, that claim would fall within another paragraph of this Practice Direction (excluding paragraphs (1) to (5), (8), (12D), (15D), (17), (22) and (24) to (25)). ## Claims by HM Revenue and Customs

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims by HM Revenue and Customs] (17) A claim is made by the Commissioners for H.M. Revenue and Customs relating to duties or taxes against a defendant not domiciled in Scotland or Northern Ireland within the meaning of sections 41 and 42 of the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982. ## Claim for costs order in favour of or against third parties

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claim for costs order in favour of or against third parties] (18) A claim is made by a party to proceedings for an order that the court exercise its power under section 51 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 to make a costs order in favour of or against a person who is not a party to those proceedings. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claim for costs order in favour of or against third parties] (Rule 46.2 sets out the procedure where the court is considering whether to exercise its discretion to make a costs order in favour of or against a non-party.)

## Admiralty claims

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Admiralty claims] (19) A claim is –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Admiralty claims] (a) in the nature of salvage and any part of the services took place within the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Admiralty claims] (b) to enforce a claim under section 153, 154,175 or 176A of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995. ## Claims under various enactments

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims under various enactments] (20) A claim is made –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims under various enactments] (a) under an enactment which allows proceedings to be brought and those proceedings are not covered by any of the other grounds referred to in this paragraph. ## Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (21) A claim is made for breach of confidence or misuse of private information where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (a) detriment was suffered, or will be suffered, within the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (b) detriment which has been, or will be, suffered results from an act committed, or likely to be committed, within the jurisdiction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (c) the obligation of confidence or right to privacy arose in the jurisdiction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (d) the obligation of confidence or right of privacy is governed by the law of England and Wales. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (22) A claim is made for a declaration that no duty of confidentiality or right to privacy has arisen where, if the duty or right was found to have arisen, it would comply with one of the conditions set out in paragraph (21)(c) or (d). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (23) A claim is made for unlawfully causing or assisting in—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (a) a breach of confidence or misuse of private information where the obligation or right in question falls within paragraph (21)(c) or (d) above; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Claims for breach of confidence or misuse of private information] (b) a breach of confidence or misuse of private information falling within paragraph (21)(a) or (b) above”. ## Contempt applications

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Contempt applications] (24) A contempt application is made, whether or not, apart from this paragraph, a claim form or application notice containing such an application can be served out of the jurisdiction. ## Information orders against non-parties

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Information orders against non-parties] (25) A claim or application is made for disclosure in order to obtain information—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Information orders against non-parties] (a) regarding:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Information orders against non-parties] (i) the true identity of a defendant or a potential defendant; and/or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Information orders against non-parties] (ii) what has become of the property of a claimant or applicant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Information orders against non-parties] (b) the claim or application is made for the purpose of proceedings already commenced or which, subject to the content of the information received, are intended to be commenced either by service in England and Wales or pursuant  to CPR rule 6.32, 6.33 or 6.36

## Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)] 4.1 A party must provide the following documents for each party to be served out of the jurisdiction –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)] (1) a copy of the particulars of claim if not already contained in or served with the claim form and any other relevant documents;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)] (2) a duplicate of the claim form, a duplicate of the particulars of claim (if not already contained in or served with the claim form), copies of any documents accompanying the claim form and copies of any other relevant documents;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)] (3) forms for responding to the claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)] (4) any translation required under rule 6.45 in duplicate. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Documents to be filed under rule 6.43(2)(c)] 4.2 Some countries require legalisation of the document to be served and some require a formal letter of request which must be signed by the Senior Master. Any queries on this should be addressed to the Foreign Process Section at the Royal Courts of Justice. ## Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] 5.1 The judicial authorities of certain Commonwealth States which are not a party to the Hague Convention require service to be in accordance with rule 6.42(1)(b)(i) and not 6.42(3). A list of such countries can be obtained from the Foreign Process Section (Room E02) at the Royal Courts of Justice. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] 5.2 The list of British overseas territories is contained in Schedule 6 to the British Nationality Act 1981. For ease of reference, these are –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (a) Anguilla;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (b) Bermuda;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (c) British Antarctic Territory;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (d) British Indian Ocean Territory;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (e) British Virgin Islands;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (f) Cayman Islands;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (g) Falkland Islands;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (h) Gibraltar;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (i) Montserrat;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (j) Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (k) St. Helena and Dependencies;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (l) South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (m) Sovereign Base Areas of Akrotiri and Dhekelia; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Service in a Commonwealth State or British overseas territory] (n) Turks and Caicos Islands. ## Period for responding to a claim form

## 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (1) file an acknowledgment of service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (2) file or serve an admission; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (3) file a defence,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] will be calculated in accordance with paragraph 6.3, 6.4 or 6.5. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] 6.2 Where the court grants permission to serve a claim form out of the jurisdiction the court will determine in accordance with paragraph 6.3, 6.4 or 6.5 the periods within which the defendant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (1) file an acknowledgment of service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (2) file or serve an admission; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (3) file a defence. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] (Rule 6.37(5)(a) provides that when giving permission to serve a claim form out of the jurisdiction the court will specify the period within which the defendant may respond to the claim form.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.1 Where rule 6.35(5) applies, the periods within which the defendant must –] 6.3 The period for filing an acknowledgment of service under Part 10 or for filing or serving an admission under Part 14 is the number of days listed in the Table after service of the particulars of claim. ## 6.4 The period for filing a defence under Part 15 is –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.4 The period for filing a defence under Part 15 is –] (1) the number of days listed in the Table after service of the particulars of claim; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.4 The period for filing a defence under Part 15 is –] (2) where the defendant has filed an acknowledgment of service, the number of days listed in the Table plus an additional 14 days after the service of the particulars of claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.4 The period for filing a defence under Part 15 is –] 6.5 Under the State Immunity Act 1978, where a State is served, the period permitted under paragraphs 6.3 and 6.4 for filing an acknowledgment of service or defence or for filing or serving an admission does not begin to run until 2 months after the date on which the State is served. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > 6.4 The period for filing a defence under Part 15 is –] 6.6 Where particulars of claim are served out of the jurisdiction any statement as to the period for responding to the claim contained in any of the forms required by rule 7.8 to accompany the particulars of claim must specify the period prescribed under rule 6.35 or by the order permitting service out of the jurisdiction under rule 6.37(5). ## Period for responding to an application notice

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Period for responding to an application notice] 7.1 Where an application notice is served out of the jurisdiction, the period for responding is 7 days less than the number of days listed in the Table. ## Further information

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 6B – SERVICE OUT OF THE JURISDICTION > Further information] 7.2 Further information concerning service out of the jurisdiction can be obtained from the Foreign Process Section, Room E02, Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London WC2A 2LL (telephone 020 7947 6691).
